clauses.why: A disclosure banner about xAI is not needed for a working bot in a development org; the request asks for no user notices.
Making the history window an administrator-tunable setting with a validated range goes beyond the request; a fixed window would serve.
Caps a conversation at 200 messages, yet lets a 199-message conversation accept a user message whose Grok answer makes 201.
A per-user rolling hourly rate limit is cost control the request never asks for; the bot works without it.
A server-side lock across tabs and devices with stale-marker expiry costs real work; disabling the panel already covers ordinary use.
An administrator on/off kill switch with its own notice is an operator feature the request does not call for.
A scheduled daily retention purge with a configurable period is housekeeping beyond the request; history can be kept or deleted manually.
Fixes a seven-setting admin surface, including enabled, hourly cap and retention, that the request does not call for.
A dedicated failed-message list view for administrators is an observability feature the request does not ask for.
Storing per-answer token usage is cost monitoring the request does not call for; the bot works without it.
Written removal steps that leave the org clean are not part of creating the bot in a development org.
The request names a development org, which has no coverage gate; 75% per-class coverage for production deployment goes beyond it.
At the highest Apex log level, variable-assignment logging records string values, so message and answer text will appear; the builder cannot prevent it.
Keyboard operation and screen-reader live-region announcements are accessibility work the request's purpose does not call for.
